bull.b: A durable, record-level bookings pipeline (4,446 jobs) provides visible near-term revenue conversion given a ~2-month median booking-to-revenue cycle. This broad backlog, supported by recent acquisitions, strengthens revenue runway and reduces reliance on spot demand over the next several quarters.

Rising ASP driven by battery attach (~$10k uplift per job) structurally raises per-installation revenue and improves unit economics. Selling storage alongside PV increases lifetime customer value and margin potential, making future revenue growth more profitable if adoption persists.

Implemented permanent cost reductions that cut OpEx by ~$9.9M/quarter improve operating leverage and lower the revenue breakeven threshold. Sustained lower fixed costs make future profitability more attainable as sales scale, reducing the sensitivity of margins to near-term revenue volatility.

bear.b: A persistent equity deficit (~-$61.5M) with sizable debt (~$156.1M) materially weakens financial flexibility and raises refinancing and solvency risk. Negative equity constrains covenant room, limits access to unsecured financing, and elevates downside risk if revenue recovery lags expectations.

bear.t: Negative operating cash flow & tight liquidity
bear.b: Sustained negative operating cash flow (~-$38M TTM) and a low reported cash balance (~$4M) create ongoing liquidity pressure. The company’s need to convert backlog rapidly to reach cash-flow breakeven increases refinancing risk and makes operations sensitive to execution delays or additional working capital needs.

Historical restatements, extensive auditor requests (~390), and a CFO departure indicate material control weaknesses. These governance issues can impair investor confidence, delay financial planning, and increase compliance and financing costs until controls are demonstrably strengthened.
